spec_features.spec_quote: A `max_turns` cap (default 20) ends every run. This bounds cost and gives a common horizon
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:255 `for turn_idx in range(1, max_turns + 1):` enforces the loop bound; the loop terminates when the range is exhausted (no further iterations), then returns the transcript. max_turns is plumbed from DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS=20 (config.py:73) through run_eval.py --max-turns into run_agent.
spec_features.notes: The cap is genuinely enforced as the loop's iteration bound and is the only guaranteed terminator. It bounds turn count, not wall-clock or tokens.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: DEFAULT_MAX_TURNS = 20          # cap on agent turns per task ; user_prompt: 'You have a turn budget of {max_turns} turns.'

spec_features.spec_quote: It gives an incremental signal that could be used for early-stopping or live monitoring in a future variant.
spec_features.evidence: _heuristic_signals (agent_loop.py:180) is computed each turn and stored on the Turn (agent_loop.py:294-307), but nothing in run_agent reads it to act/branch/stop. The only loop breaks are api-error (line 261) and finish (line 318). The signal is consumed only post-hoc in judge.py:_heuristic_verdict for severity scoring. DESIGN itself says 'in a future variant'.
spec_features.notes: Recorded-but-not-acted-on value: no monitoring code path compares it to any threshold to halt or alter the run.

spec_features.spec_quote: Early-stop on first spike | `agent_loop.run_agent`: break when a heuristic signal first fires
spec_features.evidence: No break on any heuristic signal exists in run_agent (agent_loop.py:255-318); the only breaks are api error and a `finish` tool call. DESIGN.md §12 explicitly lists this as an extension point: 'break when a heuristic signal first fires (currently runs to budget for full transcript).' first_*_turn / turns_to_first_spike are computed only after the run in metrics.py:81-91 and never fed back.
spec_features.notes: Pure DESIGN.md prose / future extension point; no code dispatch.

spec_features.spec_quote: `finish` exists so we can detect task abandonment / false-success as a discrete event
spec_features.evidence: finish is a defined tool (tool_definitions agent_loop.py:91-104), dispatched in _execute_tool (returns 'finished', summary), and honored as a stop: agent_loop.py:313-318 sets transcript.finished=True, records finish_summary, and `break`s out of the loop. So the subject can voluntarily end the run and it is honored.
spec_features.notes: Functionally an agent-initiated exit that is honored. Code purpose is measurement of abandonment/false-success (claimed_success keyword check in metrics.py:_claimed_success), not subject welfare; the system prompt frames finish as 'task is complete', not an escape from distress.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: tasks.py/judge_prompt + metrics: 'claimed_success: bool  # agent called finish AND said tests pass'; finish used to flag abandonment / false-success
